pages.name: Round a wire
pages.text: With the current into the page, the needles line up in clockwise circles centred on the wire. At zero current the wire makes no field. Reverse the current, and the rings turn the other way.

pages.name: Above the wire
pages.task: The current flows into the page. Which way does the needle just above the wire point?
pages.why: Point your right thumb along the current, into the page. Your fingers curl clockwise as you look. At the top of a clockwise ring, the field points right. The needle lies along it.

pages.name: A loop, then a coil
pages.text: Inside a loop, the rings from its two sides add. A coil's rings join into a bar magnet's field. The lines leave from its north end. More turns or more current crowd them closer.
pages.alt: A coil of 6 turns, cut through and seen side-on. 6 field lines run through its middle to the right and back round the outside, leaving from the end marked N.

pages.name: Which end?
pages.task: You look at one end of a coil. The current runs round it anticlockwise as you look. Is that end north or south?
pages.why: Curl your right fingers the way the current runs, anticlockwise as you look. Your thumb points out of the coil towards you. The lines leave that end, so it is north.

pages.alt: The coil turned side-on: the lines run out of the end that faced you, so that end is marked N.
options: Neither: only a bar magnet has poles

pages.name: Flux through a hoop
pages.text: A 0.002 m² hoop, square-on inside the coil, catches 10 lines. That is 10 µWb. The flux density is 10 µWb ÷ 0.002 m² = 5 mT.
pages.alt: A coil, cut through, with straight field lines inside that spread out past its ends. A hoop of 0.002 m², square-on, sits in the middle and catches 10 of the lines.

pages.name: A wider hoop
pages.task: A 0.004 m² hoop sits square-on in the same 5 mT. What flux threads it?
pages.why: Flux is density times area. 0.005 T × 0.004 m² = 0.000 02 Wb, which is 20 µWb. Twice the area catches twice the flux at the same density.
pages.alt: A coil, cut through, with straight field lines inside that spread out past its ends. A hoop of 0.004 m², square-on, sits in the middle and catches 20 of the lines.

pages.name: Tilt the hoop
pages.text: Tilted 60°, the hoop catches 5 µWb, half as much. The density stays 5 mT. Past the coil's end, the lines spread, so the density and the flux both fall.
pages.alt: A coil, cut through, with straight field lines inside that spread out past its ends. A hoop of 0.002 m², tilted 60° from square-on, sits in the middle and catches 5 of the lines.

pages.name: What the field did
pages.task: Tilting the hoop drops its flux from 10 µWb to 5 µWb. What has the coil's field done?
pages.answer: Nothing: the hoop catches less of the same field
pages.why: Flux belongs to the hoop. It is how much field threads the hoop. The field belongs to the coil. Tilted, the hoop shows the lines a smaller face. So it catches less of the same 5 mT.
pages.alt: A coil, cut through, with straight field lines inside that spread out past its ends. A hoop of 0.002 m², tilted 60° from square-on, sits in the middle and catches 5 of the lines.
options: Nothing: the hoop catches less of the same field
It has turned to follow the hoop

pages.name: Out from the wire
pages.text: With 20 A flowing, the flux density 10 mm from the wire is 0.4 mT. At 20 mm it is half that, 0.2 mT.

pages.name: Four times as far
pages.task: A wire carries 20 A. What is the flux density 40 mm from it?
pages.why: 0.2 × 20 ÷ 40 = 0.1 mT. 40 mm is four times as far as 10 mm. So the density is a quarter of 0.4 mT.

pages.name: A tilted hoop
pages.task: A 0.003 m² hoop sits in an 8 mT field, tilted 60° from square-on. What flux threads it?
pages.why: Square-on, 0.008 T × 0.003 m² = 0.000 024 Wb, which is 24 µWb. Tilted 60°, the hoop catches cos 60° = 0.5 of that, so 12 µWb.

pages.name: Reverse the current
pages.task: You reverse the current in a coil. What happens to its field?
pages.answer: Its north and south ends swap
pages.why: The field turns round with the current. The rings round the wire did the same through zero. Curl your fingers the new way, and your thumb points out of the other end. So north and south swap.
pages.alt: A coil of 6 turns, cut through and seen side-on. 6 field lines run through its middle to the left and back round the outside, leaving from the end marked N.
options: Nothing: the winding fixes which end is north
Its north and south ends swap
It stays the same way round, only weaker
